**Tesla – recent headlines (late Oct 2026)**  

- **Merger talks dominate** – Investors and media are treating Tesla and SpaceX as a potential mega‑merger; Musk says the deal “has a lot of merit” and would need his own approval, while analysts note the stocks of both companies moved together this summer and that the combination would be the biggest corporate merger ever [2][3][4][6][8][11].  
- **Flying Roadster unveiled** – Tesla showed a “flying” version of the Roadster equipped with SpaceX‑style thrusters, claiming it can hit 60 mph in under a second; production is slated for 2028, but traders remain skeptical after years of delays [5][14][15][16][17].  
- **Cybertruck launch cancelled in ANZ** – Tesla emailed customers on Oct 23 to announce the Cybertruck will no longer be released in Australia and New Zealand [1].  
- **Full‑Self‑Driving rebranded** – In Europe the FSD system is now marketed as “Tesla Assisted Driving,” reflecting regulatory pressure [19].  
- **Q3 profit plunge** – Tesla reported a 43 % drop in third‑quarter profits, fueling market concerns amid the merger speculation [7].  
- **Safety incident** – A Tesla on Full Self‑Driving hit and killed a pedestrian on I‑80; dash‑cam footage showed the vehicle attempted to brake and steer before the collision [9].  
- **Political spending** – Musk poured $366 million into U.S. Senate campaigns, a move tied to both Tesla and SpaceX regulatory outlooks [4].  

*These points reflect the most prominent stories from the past few weeks, with the merger narrative and the flying Roadster taking precedence over newer but less‑impactful items.*
